questions.question: Can you drive if medication impairs your ability to drive?

options.text: Yes, if you don't feel drowsy.
Yes, if a doctor prescribed it.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive if any substance impairs your driving. This includes alcohol, prescription drugs, over-the-counter drugs, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road turns sharply right, then left.
The road curves right, then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road will curve right, then curve left.

questions.question: What should you do before stopping at a red light or stop sign?

options.text: Check your mirrors for traffic around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors for traffic around you.
questions.explanation: Before stopping, check your mirrors to see the traffic around you. Stay aware of other drivers as you slow down. Then move your foot to the brake and press steadily for a smooth stop.

questions.question: A pedestrian crosses illegally in the middle of the street instead of at a crosswalk. What should you do?
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians at all times, even if they are crossing illegally.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: You must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.
You never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic traveling straight. You must always yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: What does interstate driving require?

options.text: The ability to safely drive at higher speeds.

questions.explanation: Safe interstate driving requires you to stay alert and to be able to drive at high speeds safely.

questions.question: What should you clear of snow, frost, and ice before driving?

options.text: Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.explanation: You need to see clearly through all your vehicle's windows. Clear all snow, ice, and frost from your windows and mirrors before you drive.

questions.question: A traffic light is not working. What should you do?

options.text: Stop completely and yield before entering the intersection.
If the intersection looks clear, you don't need to stop.
Drive through quickly to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and yield before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat it as an all-way stop. Come to a complete stop and yield before entering the intersection.

questions.question: An animal is on the road ahead. What should you do?
questions.explanation: When you see an animal on the road, slow down and stop if you can do so safely. Swerving can cause you to lose control and crash.

questions.question: A construction worker is signaling at a work zone. When should you follow their instructions?

options.text: Only if you see orange cones.
Unless they conflict with signs, signals, or laws.

questions.explanation: Always obey construction workers and their signals. This keeps drivers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and road workers safe.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the road mean?
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. It shows that passing is unsafe from your direction.

questions.question: Before you start the engine, you should:

options.text: Make sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.

questions.explanation: Before starting the engine, buckle your safety belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: What headlights should you use when driving in fog?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off moisture and make it harder to see.

questions.question: You have a green light and there are pedestrians in the intersection. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, you must yield to pedestrians in the intersection. Always yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: Bicyclists use hand signals because they have no turn signals. A left arm straight out means the bicyclist is turning left.

questions.question: Who must drivers obey?

options.text: Other drivers with broken-down vehicles on the road.

questions.explanation: Drivers must obey flaggers' signs and instructions. Flaggers are there to keep drivers and workers safe.

questions.question: What is distracted driving?

options.text: Anything that makes you swerve while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving means anything takes your eyes, hands, or mind off driving. It is the most common cause of traffic crashes. Any distraction stops you from seeing or hearing dangers on the road.

questions.question: When must you stop your vehicle?

options.text: When a police officer tells you to stop.
When there is a red traffic light.

questions.explanation: You must stop at a red traffic light. You must also obey a police officer directing traffic, no matter what the signs or lights say.

questions.question: When must you obey school crossing guards?
questions.explanation: Always obey school crossing guards when near a school. Watch for them and follow their instructions.

questions.question: What should you do when another vehicle is passing you?
questions.explanation: Do not speed up when being passed. Keep a steady speed so the other driver can safely pass and move back into your lane.

questions.question: Like alcohol and drugs, drowsiness can:
questions.explanation: Being tired causes poor driving. Like drugs and alcohol, sleepiness slows your reaction time, reduces awareness, and hurts your judgment.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, what must you watch for?

options.text: Vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings, like school buses and hazmat trucks.

questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with great caution. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. Watch for vehicles like school buses and hazmat trucks that must stop at all railroad crossings.

questions.question: Why is night driving harder?

options.text: The speed limit is higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the road at night.
It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.
questions.explanation: Night driving has special problems. The dark makes it hard to judge how far away things are and how fast other vehicles are going. You can only see as far as your headlights reach.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A round sign means a railroad crossing is ahead. It is posted a few hundred feet before the tracks. It tells drivers to slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A side road meets the main road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A side road meets the main road ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to dangers ahead. They are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that a side road will meet the main road ahead. Be alert and ready.

questions.question: What should you do if you get tired while driving?

options.text: Stop to rest or let someone else drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: Stop to rest or switch drivers if you become tired. Tiredness slows your thinking and reactions, which makes driving unsafe.

questions.question: Which of these dangerous driving practices is also illegal?

options.text: Wearing headphones in both ears while driving.
Transporting an unsecured animal in the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing headphones in both ears while driving.
questions.explanation: Do not wear headsets or earplugs in both ears while driving. It is illegal. You cannot hear important sounds if both ears are blocked.

questions.question: What should you do if the road is wet or icy?
questions.explanation: Your tires do not grip the road as well when it is wet, snowy, or icy. Slow down on wet or icy roads.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A steep downhill slope is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep downhill slope is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a steep downhill slope ahead. Check your brakes before going down.

questions.question: Is it legal to smoke in a vehicle with someone under 18 inside?

options.text: Yes, if it is your child.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to smoke in a vehicle when a minor is inside.
